11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(1)
The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $27,900 in value, in real property or personal property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, in a cooperative that owns property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, or in a burial plot for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(8)
Equity in one motor vehicle of not more than $15,000.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(9)
Professionally prescribed prostheses for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, including a wheelchair or motorized mobility device.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10)
All firearms of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(11)
All domestic animals or household pets.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(1)
The tools, equipment, instruments and books, including telephone numbers, client or customer contact information, or marketing tools, such as websites, domain names or any other intangible work product, in the possession of a debtor or the spouse of a debtor primarily used in, and necessary to carry on or develop, the commercial activity, trade, business or profession of the debtor or the debtor's spouse, not in excess of an aggregate fair market value of five thousand dollars. For the purpose of this paragraph, tools do not include a motor vehicle primarily used by a debtor for personal, family or household purposes such as transportation to and from the debtor's place of employment.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(2)
Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(c)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $2,400 in value, in any one motor vehicle;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(d)
The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $1,500 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools of the trade of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(e)
Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

Oregon Revised Statutes
Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. The following property, or rights or interest therein of the judgment debtor, shall be exempt from execution:

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(d)
A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(3)
If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. The exemptions provided by subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d), (j), (k) and (p) of this section, when claimed for jointly owned property, may be combined at the option of the debtors.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.362
Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(2)
The exemption shall extend to the proceeds derived from such sale to an amount not exceeding $40,000 or $50,000, whichever amount is applicable under subsection (1) of this section, if the proceeds are held for a period not exceeding one year and held with the intention to procure another homestead therewith.

Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123
General monetary exemption. General rule.--In addition to any other property specifically exempted by this subchapter, property of the judgment debtor (including bank notes, money, securities, real property, judgments or other indebtedness due the judgment debtor) to the value of $300 shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment. Within such time as may be prescribed by general rules the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in kind and may designate the specific items of property to which the exemption provided by this section shall be applicable unless the designated property is not capable of appropriate division, or the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in cash out of the proceeds of the sale. For married persons, each spouse is entitled to the exemptions provided in this section.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)
Exemption of particular property. Goods.--The following personal property of the judgment debtor shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment:

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(1)
Wearing apparel.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(2)
Bibles and school books.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(3)
Sewing machines belonging to seamstresses or used and owned by private families, but not including sewing machines kept for sale or hire.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(4)
The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

Wisconsin Statutes
Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)
Exempt property. The debtor's interest in or right to receive the following property is exempt:

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(a)
Provisions for burial. Cemetery lots, aboveground burial facilities, burial monuments, tombstones, coffins, cremation urns, urn vaults, outer burial containers, or other articles for the burial of the dead owned by the debtor and intended for the burial of the debtor or the debtor's family.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)
Business and farm property.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)(1)
Equipment, inventory, farm products, and professional books used in the business of the debtor or the business of a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)(2)
If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(d)
Consumer goods. Household goods and furnishings, wearing apparel, keepsakes, jewelry and other articles of personal adornment, appliances, books, musical instruments, firearms, sporting goods, animals, or other tangible personal property held primarily for the personal, family or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $12,000 in aggregate value.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g)
Motor vehicles. Motor vehicles not to exceed $4,000 in aggregate value. Any unused amount of the aggregate value from par. (d) may be added to this exemption to increase the aggregate exempt value of motor vehicles under this paragraph.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(k)
Depository accounts. Depository accounts in the aggregate value of $5,000, but only to the extent that the account is for the debtor's personal use and is not used as a business account.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(8)
Marital property rights. Each spouse is entitled to and may claim the exemptions under this section. If the property exempt under this section is limited to a specified maximum dollar amount, each spouse is entitled to one exemption. That exemption is limited to the specified maximum dollar amount, which may be combined with the other spouse's exemption in the same property or applied to different property included under the same exemption.

Wis. Stat. § 815.20
Homestead exemption definition.

Wis. Stat. § 815.20(1)
An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided. The exemption shall not be impaired by temporary removal with the intention to reoccupy the premises as a homestead nor by the sale of the homestead, but shall extend to the proceeds derived from the sale to an amount not exceeding $75,000, while held, with the intention to procure another homestead with the proceeds, for 2 years. The exemption extends to land owned by husband and wife jointly or in common or as marital property, and each spouse may claim a homestead exemption of not more than $75,000. The exemption extends to the interest therein of tenants in common, having a homestead thereon with the consent of the cotenants, and to any estate less than a fee.

raw_block.rationale: Adds a compact airline terminal helper that avoids the repeatedly unresolved multi-scalar fee schedule. outputs.description: The exact integer ticket price plus the complete charges for every current checked bag.

An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided. # Bag fees
All published bag fees apply at each check-in location and are base rates according to travel dates and destination; applicable taxes are not shown.

## Carry-on bags
You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.

### Personal items
Your personal item like a purse or small handbag must fit under the seat in front of you. Dimensions should not exceed 18 x 14 x 8 inches (45 x 35 x 20 cm).

These don't count as your personal item or carry-on:
* Diaper bags (1 per child)
* Breast pump
* Small, soft-sided cooler of breast milk
* Child safety seats, strollers and medical or mobility devices

### Carry-on items
You can bring only one carry-on item along with your personal item. Your carry-on must fit in in the overhead bin or under the seat in front of you. If it doesn't fit, it will need to be checked. Be sure all your carry-on items are labeled in case they are checked.

#### Carry-on bag
The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.

#### Soft-sided garment bag
Your soft-sided garment bag cannot exceed 51 inches / 130 cm (length + width + height).

Bag fees have been updated effective for tickets issued on / after February 20, 2024.

Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Homestead exemption. General monetary exemption. General rule.--In addition to any other property specifically exempted by this subchapter, property of the judgment debtor (including bank notes, money, securities, real property, judgments or other indebtedness due the judgment debtor) to the value of $300 shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment. The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

Business and farm property.

Equipment, inventory, farm products, and professional books used in the business of the debtor or the business of a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value.

If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Consumer goods. Marital property rights. Each spouse is entitled to and may claim the exemptions under this section. raw_block.rationale: Aggregate the two legally distinct baggage components before arithmetic: ordinal checked-bag base fees and the per-bag higher-of-oversize-or-overweight charges. Scalar totals avoid the array-alignment failures seen in prior drafts while preserving the governing fee-combination rule.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated in the current facts?

inputs.name: checked_bag_base_fee_total
inputs.question: After allocating at most one qualifying carry-on and one qualifying personal item, what is the total of the ordinal checked-bag base fees selected from the detailed rows matching the current route and cabin?

inputs.name: higher_excess_fee_total
inputs.question: Across all current checked bags, what is the total obtained by taking for each bag only the higher applicable oversize or overweight fee, using zero when neither applies and applying any complimentary-bag weight allowance only where the current source grants it?

skill.intent: Compute the exact current ticket-plus-baggage total from separately determined checked-bag base-fee and higher-excess-fee totals.

outputs.description: The exact integer ticket price plus all current checked-bag base and applicable excess fees.
outputs.name: answer

fields.name: higher_excess_fee_total
fields.question: What is the total of the per-bag higher applicable oversize or overweight fees for those checked bags?

support.text:
11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(1)
The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $27,900 in value, in real property or personal property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, in a cooperative that owns property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, or in a burial plot for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(8)
Equity in one motor vehicle of not more than $15,000.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(9)
Professionally prescribed prostheses for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, including a wheelchair or motorized mobility device.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10)
All firearms of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(11)
All domestic animals or household pets.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(1)
The tools, equipment, instruments and books, including telephone numbers, client or customer contact information, or marketing tools, such as websites, domain names or any other intangible work product, in the possession of a debtor or the spouse of a debtor primarily used in, and necessary to carry on or develop, the commercial activity, trade, business or profession of the debtor or the debtor's spouse, not in excess of an aggregate fair market value of five thousand dollars. For the purpose of this paragraph, tools do not include a motor vehicle primarily used by a debtor for personal, family or household purposes such as transportation to and from the debtor's place of employment.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(2)
Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(c)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $2,400 in value, in any one motor vehicle;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(d)
The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $1,500 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools of the trade of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(e)
Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

Oregon Revised Statutes
Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. The following property, or rights or interest therein of the judgment debtor, shall be exempt from execution:

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(d)
A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(3)
If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. The exemptions provided by subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d), (j), (k) and (p) of this section, when claimed for jointly owned property, may be combined at the option of the debtors.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.362
Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Professionally prescribed prostheses for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, including a wheelchair or motorized mobility device.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10)
All firearms of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(11)
All domestic animals or household pets.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(1)
The tools, equipment, instruments and books, including telephone numbers, client or customer contact information, or marketing tools, such as websites, domain names or any other intangible work product, in the possession of a debtor or the spouse of a debtor primarily used in, and necessary to carry on or develop, the commercial activity, trade, business or profession of the debtor or the debtor's spouse, not in excess of an aggregate fair market value of five thousand dollars. The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

Oregon Revised Statutes
Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. The following property, or rights or interest therein of the judgment debtor, shall be exempt from execution:

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(d)
A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(3)
If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. The exemptions provided by subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d), (j), (k) and (p) of this section, when claimed for jointly owned property, may be combined at the option of the debtors.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.362
Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(2)
The exemption shall extend to the proceeds derived from such sale to an amount not exceeding $40,000 or $50,000, whichever amount is applicable under subsection (1) of this section, if the proceeds are held for a period not exceeding one year and held with the intention to procure another homestead therewith.

Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123
General monetary exemption. General rule.--In addition to any other property specifically exempted by this subchapter, property of the judgment debtor (including bank notes, money, securities, real property, judgments or other indebtedness due the judgment debtor) to the value of $300 shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment. Within such time as may be prescribed by general rules the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in kind and may designate the specific items of property to which the exemption provided by this section shall be applicable unless the designated property is not capable of appropriate division, or the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in cash out of the proceeds of the sale. For married persons, each spouse is entitled to the exemptions provided in this section.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)
Exemption of particular property. Goods.--The following personal property of the judgment debtor shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment:

Wearing apparel.

Bibles and school books.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(3)
Sewing machines belonging to seamstresses or used and owned by private families, but not including sewing machines kept for sale or hire.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(4)
The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

Business and farm property.

If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Consumer goods. Household goods and furnishings, wearing apparel, keepsakes, jewelry and other articles of personal adornment, appliances, books, musical instruments, firearms, sporting goods, animals, or other tangible personal property held primarily for the personal, family or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $12,000 in aggregate value.

Motor vehicles. Motor vehicles not to exceed $4,000 in aggregate value. Any unused amount of the aggregate value from par. (d) may be added to this exemption to increase the aggregate exempt value of motor vehicles under this paragraph.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(k)
Depository accounts. Depository accounts in the aggregate value of $5,000, but only to the extent that the account is for the debtor's personal use and is not used as a business account.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(8)
Marital property rights. Each spouse is entitled to and may claim the exemptions under this section. An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided. Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

Oregon Revised Statutes
Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. The following property, or rights or interest therein of the judgment debtor, shall be exempt from execution:

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(d)
A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(3)
If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. The exemptions provided by subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d), (j), (k) and (p) of this section, when claimed for jointly owned property, may be combined at the option of the debtors.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.362
Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(2)
The exemption shall extend to the proceeds derived from such sale to an amount not exceeding $40,000 or $50,000, whichever amount is applicable under subsection (1) of this section, if the proceeds are held for a period not exceeding one year and held with the intention to procure another homestead therewith.

Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123
General monetary exemption. General rule.--In addition to any other property specifically exempted by this subchapter, property of the judgment debtor (including bank notes, money, securities, real property, judgments or other indebtedness due the judgment debtor) to the value of $300 shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment. Within such time as may be prescribed by general rules the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in kind and may designate the specific items of property to which the exemption provided by this section shall be applicable unless the designated property is not capable of appropriate division, or the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in cash out of the proceeds of the sale. For married persons, each spouse is entitled to the exemptions provided in this section.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)
Exemption of particular property. Goods.--The following personal property of the judgment debtor shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment:

Wearing apparel.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(2)
Bibles and school books.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(3)
Sewing machines belonging to seamstresses or used and owned by private families, but not including sewing machines kept for sale or hire.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(4)
The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

Wisconsin Statutes
Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)
Exempt property. The debtor's interest in or right to receive the following property is exempt:

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(a)
Provisions for burial. Cemetery lots, aboveground burial facilities, burial monuments, tombstones, coffins, cremation urns, urn vaults, outer burial containers, or other articles for the burial of the dead owned by the debtor and intended for the burial of the debtor or the debtor's family.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)
Business and farm property.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)(1)
Equipment, inventory, farm products, and professional books used in the business of the debtor or the business of a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)(2)
If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(d)
Consumer goods. Household goods and furnishings, wearing apparel, keepsakes, jewelry and other articles of personal adornment, appliances, books, musical instruments, firearms, sporting goods, animals, or other tangible personal property held primarily for the personal, family or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $12,000 in aggregate value.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g)
Motor vehicles. Motor vehicles not to exceed $4,000 in aggregate value. Any unused amount of the aggregate value from par. (d) may be added to this exemption to increase the aggregate exempt value of motor vehicles under this paragraph.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(k)
Depository accounts. Depository accounts in the aggregate value of $5,000, but only to the extent that the account is for the debtor's personal use and is not used as a business account.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(8)
Marital property rights. Each spouse is entitled to and may claim the exemptions under this section. If the property exempt under this section is limited to a specified maximum dollar amount, each spouse is entitled to one exemption. That exemption is limited to the specified maximum dollar amount, which may be combined with the other spouse's exemption in the same property or applied to different property included under the same exemption.

Homestead exemption definition.

An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided. support.text:
11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(1)
The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $27,900 in value, in real property or personal property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, in a cooperative that owns property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, or in a burial plot for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(8)
Equity in one motor vehicle of not more than $15,000.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(9)
Professionally prescribed prostheses for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, including a wheelchair or motorized mobility device.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10)
All firearms of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(11)
All domestic animals or household pets.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(1)
The tools, equipment, instruments and books, including telephone numbers, client or customer contact information, or marketing tools, such as websites, domain names or any other intangible work product, in the possession of a debtor or the spouse of a debtor primarily used in, and necessary to carry on or develop, the commercial activity, trade, business or profession of the debtor or the debtor's spouse, not in excess of an aggregate fair market value of five thousand dollars. For the purpose of this paragraph, tools do not include a motor vehicle primarily used by a debtor for personal, family or household purposes such as transportation to and from the debtor's place of employment.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(2)
Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(c)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $2,400 in value, in any one motor vehicle;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(d)
The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $1,500 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools of the trade of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(e)
Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

Oregon Revised Statutes
Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. The following property, or rights or interest therein of the judgment debtor, shall be exempt from execution:

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(d)
A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(3)
If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. The exemptions provided by subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d), (j), (k) and (p) of this section, when claimed for jointly owned property, may be combined at the option of the debtors.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.362
Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(2)
The exemption shall extend to the proceeds derived from such sale to an amount not exceeding $40,000 or $50,000, whichever amount is applicable under subsection (1) of this section, if the proceeds are held for a period not exceeding one year and held with the intention to procure another homestead therewith.

Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes
42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123
General monetary exemption. General rule.--In addition to any other property specifically exempted by this subchapter, property of the judgment debtor (including bank notes, money, securities, real property, judgments or other indebtedness due the judgment debtor) to the value of $300 shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment. Within such time as may be prescribed by general rules the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in kind and may designate the specific items of property to which the exemption provided by this section shall be applicable unless the designated property is not capable of appropriate division, or the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in cash out of the proceeds of the sale. For married persons, each spouse is entitled to the exemptions provided in this section.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)
Exemption of particular property. Goods.--The following personal property of the judgment debtor shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment:

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(1)
Wearing apparel.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(2)
Bibles and school books.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(3)
Sewing machines belonging to seamstresses or used and owned by private families, but not including sewing machines kept for sale or hire.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8124(a)(4)
The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

Wisconsin Statutes
Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)
Exempt property. The debtor's interest in or right to receive the following property is exempt:

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(a)
Provisions for burial. Cemetery lots, aboveground burial facilities, burial monuments, tombstones, coffins, cremation urns, urn vaults, outer burial containers, or other articles for the burial of the dead owned by the debtor and intended for the burial of the debtor or the debtor's family.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)
Business and farm property.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)(1)
Equipment, inventory, farm products, and professional books used in the business of the debtor or the business of a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(b)(2)
If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(d)
Consumer goods. Household goods and furnishings, wearing apparel, keepsakes, jewelry and other articles of personal adornment, appliances, books, musical instruments, firearms, sporting goods, animals, or other tangible personal property held primarily for the personal, family or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $12,000 in aggregate value.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g)
Motor vehicles. Motor vehicles not to exceed $4,000 in aggregate value. Any unused amount of the aggregate value from par. (d) may be added to this exemption to increase the aggregate exempt value of motor vehicles under this paragraph.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(k)
Depository accounts. Depository accounts in the aggregate value of $5,000, but only to the extent that the account is for the debtor's personal use and is not used as a business account.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(8)

Jose Ortiz (hereinafter the Debtor) filed for bankruptcy on 7th of September 2024. Records show that Jose possesses a wall-mounted floating shelf made of reclaimed barn wood with a value of $800.00. Ownership of the hooded fleece robe with belt and two front pockets, priced at $105.00, is claimed by the Debtor.

support.text:
11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1123
Household furniture, furnishings and appliances. Household furniture and furnishings, household goods, including consumer electronic devices, and household appliances personally used by the debtor or a dependent of the debtor and not otherwise specifically prescribed in this chapter are exempt from process provided their aggregate fair market value does not exceed $15,000.

Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

The exemption shall extend to the proceeds derived from such sale to an amount not exceeding $40,000 or $50,000, whichever amount is applicable under subsection (1) of this section, if the proceeds are held for a period not exceeding one year and held with the intention to procure another homestead therewith.

The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Motor vehicles. Motor vehicles not to exceed $4,000 in aggregate value. Any unused amount of the aggregate value from par. (d) may be added to this exemption to increase the aggregate exempt value of motor vehicles under this paragraph.

Depository accounts. Depository accounts in the aggregate value of $5,000, but only to the extent that the account is for the debtor's personal use and is not used as a business account.

Marital property rights. Each spouse is entitled to and may claim the exemptions under this section. Homestead exemption definition.

An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided. The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

All domestic animals or household pets.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(2)
Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $1,500 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools of the trade of the debtor;

Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.362
Exemption for firearms. Every person above the age of 16 years shall be entitled to have, hold and keep, for the own use and defense of the person and shall have exempt from execution one rifle, shotgun or pistol. The value of firearms claimed as exempt under this section may not exceed $1,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(1)
Homestead exemption. A homestead shall be exempt from sale on execution, from the lien of every judgment and from liability in any form for the debts of the owner to the amount in value of $40,000, except as otherwise provided by law. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.395(2)
The exemption shall extend to the proceeds derived from such sale to an amount not exceeding $40,000 or $50,000, whichever amount is applicable under subsection (1) of this section, if the proceeds are held for a period not exceeding one year and held with the intention to procure another homestead therewith.

42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123
General monetary exemption. General rule.--In addition to any other property specifically exempted by this subchapter, property of the judgment debtor (including bank notes, money, securities, real property, judgments or other indebtedness due the judgment debtor) to the value of $300 shall be exempt from attachment or execution on a judgment. Within such time as may be prescribed by general rules the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in kind and may designate the specific items of property to which the exemption provided by this section shall be applicable unless the designated property is not capable of appropriate division, or the judgment debtor may claim the exemption in cash out of the proceeds of the sale. For married persons, each spouse is entitled to the exemptions provided in this section.

Wearing apparel.

Bibles and school books.

Sewing machines belonging to seamstresses or used and owned by private families, but not including sewing machines kept for sale or hire.

The uniform and accoutrements of every commissioned officer and enlisted person shall be free from all suits, distresses, executions or sales for debt or payment of taxes.

Business and farm property.

Equipment, inventory, farm products, and professional books used in the business of the debtor or the business of a dependent of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value.

If the debtor does not claim an exemption under subd. 1., any interest of the debtor, not to exceed $15,000 in aggregate value, in a closely held business that employs the debtor or in whose business the debtor is actively involved.

Consumer goods. Motor vehicles. Motor vehicles not to exceed $4,000 in aggregate value. Any unused amount of the aggregate value from par. (d) may be added to this exemption to increase the aggregate exempt value of motor vehicles under this paragraph.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(k)
Depository accounts. Depository accounts in the aggregate value of $5,000, but only to the extent that the account is for the debtor's personal use and is not used as a business account.

Wis. Stat. § 815.18(8)
Marital property rights. Each spouse is entitled to and may claim the exemptions under this section. An exempt homestead selected by a resident owner and occupied by him or her shall be exempt from execution, from the lien of every judgment, and from liability for the debts of the owner to the amount of $75,000, except mortgages, laborers', mechanics', and purchase money liens and taxes and except as otherwise provided.
